$description: ⑨ The Inspector dock's own chrome, as a Jx document over the kit: a header naming what the dock is pointed at, a real `tablist` of four tabs, and four `tabpanel`s. It draws no tab BODY — all four are mounted documents of their own (`surfaces/properties-panel.json`, `surfaces/style-panel.json`, `surfaces/logic-panel.json`, and the assistant's) — so each panel carries one empty `[part="panel-body"]` island the adapter announces through `onNodeCreated` (studio-ui-guidelines.md §9.4). The four panels are keyed on the tab id and the id list never changes, so a body host is created ONCE and lives as long as the dock: that is what the old module's hand-built permanent containers were for, and it is now a property of a keyed `$map` rather than a rule someone has to keep. `panels/right-panel.ts` keeps every decision — which tab is selected, per document or detached; what the target's name is; and which of the four seams a host is handed to.

style.$description: `styles/inspector.css`'s dock rules, carried in. Three of them were `#right-panel > .panel-*` — a direct-child selector that only held while this module rendered flat into the shell cell — and they are `[part]` rules on the document's own children now, which is the same statement without depending on how deep the dock is mounted. The header's typography is `panels.css`'s `.panel-header*`, at the same values: `--spectrum-font-size-50` resolved only inside `<sp-theme>` and a document mounts outside it, so it is `--jx-text-sm` (11px) here.

::before.$description: The separator between the tab's name and its target, drawn rather than written into the string — `panels/right-panel.ts` states what the dock is pointed at and nothing about punctuation.

& [part=\"tabs\"].$description: Four words in a 280px dock, allowed to compress rather than to become anonymous — which is why the tabs are not icons (§3.2 ⑨). The kit tab's own 220px cap would let one tab push the last off the strip, so each takes an equal quarter.

& [part=\"panel\"].$description: `#right-panel > .panel-body { flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto }`. The kit's tab panel pads itself for a dialog; a dock's tab is the whole column and each body pads its own content.

& [part=\"panel\"][data-tab=\"assistant\.$description: The chat owns its own scrolling, so its panel is a nested flex column that does not scroll.

children.$description: The island. Every one of the four tabs is a mounted document of its own, so this stays EMPTY for the life of the dock — `panels/right-panel.ts` is handed it through `onNodeCreated` and passes it to that tab's binder exactly once. It is a slotted child rather than the panel element itself because `jx-tab-panel` distributes its own slot, and a second owner of that child list would fight it.
